chapters.title: The Power of Purposeful Practice
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening chapter introduces purposeful practice through Steve Faloon digit-memory training and contrasts naive repetition with specific goals, focus, feedback, stretch, and method changes after plateaus.
chapters.coreMove: Replace broad repetition with one narrow, feedback-rich target that forces the next attempt to change.
chapters.commonMisread: Practice more, stay consistent, and effort will eventually compound.

chapters.title: Harnessing Adaptability
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter explains that bodies and minds adapt under repeated demand, so apparent limits can move, but the adaptation follows the training pattern whether useful or harmful.
chapters.coreMove: Diagnose what a training demand is actually teaching before trusting strain as improvement.
chapters.commonMisread: Any discomfort means growth and every limit is fake.

chapters.title: Mental Representations
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter claims experts perform better because rich domain-specific mental representations change what they notice, remember, predict, and correct.
chapters.coreMove: Turn practice into the construction and testing of a better inner model of the task.
chapters.commonMisread: Experts are simply faster, smarter, or better memorizers.

chapters.title: The Gold Standard
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter defines deliberate practice as the strongest form where clear standards, skilled coaching, focused repetition, stretch, and immediate feedback are available.
chapters.coreMove: Borrow or build a proven practice structure instead of guessing what serious effort should look like.
chapters.commonMisread: Deliberate practice just means working hard on something difficult.

chapters.title: Principles of Deliberate Practice on the Job
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter transfers deliberate-practice logic into messy workplaces through subskill isolation, designed feedback loops, review habits, and self-diagnosis without pretending work is a clean training field.
chapters.coreMove: Carve one repeatable subskill out of live work and install feedback close enough to alter the next attempt.
chapters.commonMisread: Experience and busy days naturally create expertise.

chapters.title: Principles of Deliberate Practice in Everyday Life
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter adapts deliberate-practice principles for ordinary learners by using narrow goals, created feedback, repeated review, and anti-vagueness discipline when formal coaching is weak.
chapters.coreMove: Shrink an ordinary activity into a visible standard, a short rep, and a feedback signal you can use immediately.
chapters.commonMisread: Daily habit, enthusiasm, or time spent is enough to improve everyday skill.

chapters.title: The Road to Extraordinary
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter explains that extraordinary performance grows through a long developmental road with rising standards, deepening commitment, accumulating gains, and real costs.
chapters.coreMove: Build a support system that keeps focused practice alive through the long middle after easy gains fade.
chapters.commonMisread: Greatness comes from heroic drive or a single breakthrough season.

chapters.title: But What About Natural Talent?
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter handles the strongest objection: talent and biology matter, but high performance cannot be explained by talent alone because training history, selection effects, support, and response variation distort the story.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a talent claim into an investigation of training history, access, selection, and response before accepting a fixed ceiling.
chapters.commonMisread: Talent is either everything or nothing.

chapters.title: Where Do We Go from Here?
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing chapter argues that education, workplaces, and institutions should change if human performance is more trainable than static talent stories suggest, with concrete standards and support structures.
chapters.coreMove: Redesign environments so practice, coaching, opportunity, and standards are built into the system rather than left to private luck.
chapters.commonMisread: Be optimistic about human potential and encourage everyone more.
